text:
mike: Heads-up - after promoting tanager-mini-q4 to canary we see a small but consistent class of schema parse failures on tool-invoke (~0.45%). dash: https://dash.internal/runs/5078
tara: sample payloads? is it truncation, extra chars, or encoding?
diego: i pulled a few failed streams. pattern: JSON looks valid but schema validator fails because of invisible characters inside string fields. example visible snippet: '{\"id\":123,\"text\":\"New user signed up\" }' — but when hex-dumped there's a U+FEFF (BOM) or zero-width space between words: "New\uFEFF user". validator library treats those as non-normalized and schema rejects.
anya: wow. where are those coming from? kernel instrumentation? tokenizer? client?
diego: correlates with int4 quant path + streaming + kv-cache. we saw these more when fallback kernels were hit. hypothesis: some debug trace injection uses a zero-width marker (for internal delimiting) that didn't get stripped and can split across stream chunks producing invisible code points inside strings.
tara: repro steps i used: canary with stream=true and long context (~900 tokens) + kv-cache. ci-bot attached small repro:```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.internal/invoke \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' \
  -d '{"model":"tanager-mini-q4","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"(lot of text)..."}],"tools":[{"id":"track_event","schema":{}}]}'
```
mike: what about retries? did retry cause duplicates?
diego: yes a few Dedicated tenants retried on 400 and we observed duplicate events (~0.01%). ops-bot flagged tenant: data-scout.
ops-bot: tenant data-scout reported duplicate track_event rows twice. recommend: avoid retrying 4xx schema/parsing errors and add idempotency_key for side-effecting tools.
anya: quick mitigation i did: pre-parse normalization to NFKC and strip known invisible chars (U+FEFF, U+200B, U+2060). small python snippet:```python
import unicodedata
clean = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', raw)
clean = clean.replace('\uFEFF', '').replace('\u200B', '').replace('\u2060', '')
```
this fixes the samples in canary.
tara: we should be careful: normalization might change user-provided strings. but for internal tool fields we control schema; seems acceptable as runtime sanitizer behind a FF.
mike: longer-term: remove debug delimiting markers from production kernels and make sure any debug-only markers are never routed to streaming output. also add unit tests for invisible char injection across chunk boundaries.
diego: i'll add streaming unit that yields chunks splitting a zero-width space between characters and assert sanitizer recovers. will put under eng-ml/stream-tests.
ci-bot: created job: https://ci.internal/job/5078/zero-width-fuzz (fuzzes insertion at all offsets)
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy: runtime-invisible-sanitize -> tanager canary at 5078901260, rollout 10% -> 100% in 15m if green
anya: also note: some clients might legitimately use zero-width joiners for languages; we need to scope sanitizer to tool output fields only, not end-user message content. add tagging in runtime to only sanitize tool payloads.
mike: good call. action items: (1) infra: runtime sanitizer FF-limited to tool outputs (tara) (2) kernel: remove delimiting markers in prod builds (diego) (3) eng-ml: add fuzz+unit tests for invisible-char chunk-splits (diego) (4) platform: update retry policy to not retry 4xx parse errors + idempotency RFC for tools (mike + product) (5) ops: notify affected Dedicated tenant and check for SLA impact (ops-bot)
tara: opening PRs now for runtime sanitizer and test harness. link when ready.
diego: kernel patch WIP, will post link.
ops-bot: tenant contact info posted privately. no major SLA breaches yet but monitoring.
mike: thanks. keeping this thread as the coordination point. ping me @mike for trace access or tenant handoff.
